body.value: 郡一　藤津郡東分　郷二　鹿島郷　能古見郷　村三十五　町五　宿二　津五　潟
郡（ぐん）一、藤津郡（ふじつぐん）東分（ひがしぶん）／郷（ごう）二、鹿島郷（かしまごう）・能古見郷（のごみごう）／村（むら）三十五／町（まち）五／宿（しゅく）二／津（つ）五／潟（かた）〔數の記載なし〕

Districts and settlements of Kashima domain: 1 district, the eastern portion of Fujitsu; 2 rural townships, Kashima-gō and Nokomi-gō; 35 villages; 5 towns; 2 post-stations; 5 harbours; and 潟 (tidal lagoon or reclaimed inlet), for which the page prints the word with no numeral after it. The three columns form one continuous listing, and all of them stand to the right of the ○鴨方藩 marker, so they close Kashima's block rather than opening Kamogata's. MASTER records 潟一; the paper below 潟 is blank, so the count is absent from the source.
郡村（鹿島藩）
（十二小隊　ヲ二大隊ト爲　人員四百人）
（十二小隊（じゅうにしょうたい）を二大隊（にだいたい）と為（な）す、人員（じんいん）四百人）

Troops of Kashima domain, printed in parentheses with a two-column interlinear note: twelve companies, which are combined into two battalions; total strength 400 men. The whole entry sits to the right of the ○鴨方藩 marker and therefore belongs to Kashima. The source writes the verb in characters as 爲; MASTER renders the same sentence with the kana トシ.
兵隊十二小隊（鹿島藩分）
○鴨方藩
○鴨方藩（かもがたはん）

Domain marker: Kamogata han, a 25,000-koku branch house of the Ikeda of Okayama, in Bitchū province. The marker opens Kamogata's entry: every column to its left on this leaf is Kamogata's, every column to its right belongs to Kashima.
○鴨方藩
草高　二萬五千石
草高（くさだか）　二万五千石（にまんごせんごく）

Nominal assessed yield (kusadaka): 25,000 koku — the register figure on which Kamogata's status as a domain rested. The page prints the plain numeral 二; MASTER's transcription uses the formal 貳, but the value is the same.
草高
外　八百三十九石七斗七升　新田改出
外（ほか）　八百三十九石七斗七升（はっぴゃくさんじゅうきゅうこく ななと ななしょう）　新田改出（しんでんあらためだし）

In addition to the nominal assessment: 839.77 koku, entered as newly reclaimed paddy brought onto the register by re-survey (shinden aratamedashi). The small character 外 at the head of the column marks the figure as an addition standing outside the kusadaka.
込高新田改出
合高　二萬五千八百三十九石七斗七升
合高（ごうだか）　二万五千八百三十九石七斗七升

Combined assessment: 25,839.77 koku. This is the sum of the two preceding columns — 25,000 koku of nominal assessment plus 839.77 koku of newly reclaimed paddy — and the two components reconcile with the total exactly.
合高
五ヶ年平均
五ヶ年平均（ごかねんへいきん）
Heading standing to the right of the tax entries: the rice and cash figures that follow are five-year averages, not a single year's receipts.
五ヶ年平均
正租　現米　一米九千二百十六石九斗八升四合六勺
正租（せいそ）　現米（げんまい）　一（ひとつ）、米（こめ）九千二百十六石九斗八升四合六勺

Regular land tax, stated in genmai (net hulled rice) and averaged over five years: first item, rice, 9,216.9846 koku. Set against the combined assessment of 25,839.77 koku on this same leaf, the domain took roughly 35.7 percent of the registered yield. The box encloses the heading 正租, the small interlinear gloss 現米 that specifies the measure, and the figure itself. MASTER's parsed value carries an extra decimal place that its own transcription does not contain; the printed sub-units read 九斗八升四合六勺, giving .9846.
正租現米
一金五兩永四百八十九文五分
一（ひとつ）、金（きん）五両（ごりょう）　永（えい）四百八十九文五分（よんひゃくはちじゅうきゅうもん ごぶ）

Cash item under the same five-year-average tax block: 5 ryō in gold, plus 489.5 mon reckoned in eiraku cash. Note that the page prints no separate 雜税 (miscellaneous tax) heading — the line simply follows the rice item as the second enumerated entry under 正租 — so the label under which the dataset files this figure is an editorial inference rather than something printed on the leaf.
雜稅金
產物　鹽　無稅
産物（さんぶつ）　塩（しお）　無税（むぜい）
Products: salt — untaxed. Kamogata's coastal salt pans on the Inland Sea are the one commodity the survey records for the domain, and it reports no levy on them.
產物鹽
藩制一覧表第三 （鴨方）
藩制一覧表第三（はんせいいちらんひょう だいさん）（鴨方（かもがた））

Running header, giving the provenance of the leaf: Han Governance Survey, Fascicle 3, Kamogata section. The header names the fascicle and the domain whose section the leaf falls in, which here is also the domain that owns most of the data on it.
藩制一覧表第三（鴨方）
百八十一
百八十一（ひゃくはちじゅういち）＝181
Printed book page number in the bottom margin: 181.
本書頁番号（鴨方藩分）
